chunk_findings.detail: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim (`f"  [!] {t}"` for `t in r["stranded"]`), i.e. it assumes the status dict carries plain strings, exactly like `_health_lines` does for `r["health"]`. But the change's own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) asserts that the very same field, read back from `ddflow --json status`, is a list of *dicts*: `rows = json.loads(out)["stranded"]`, `[r["item"] for r in rows]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`. Since the human and `--json` surfaces are fed by the same status dict produced by `ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py` (the other accessors in `_print_status` — `r["ready"]`, `r["waiting"]`, `r["health"]` — are likewise the shared dict), the two shapes cannot both be right. With the JSON shape the human line prints a raw Python representation of the dict, e.g. `  [!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': '...'}`, instead of the message that `stranded_text` produced; the test does not catch it because it only checks for the substrings `"Removed, lease still held"` and `"T2"`, both of which survive inside the dict repr. The line should render `t["text"]` (or the status builder should store strings), otherwise `ddflow status` shows internal structure to the user in both clones, including the holder's clone where the intended `ddflow release T2` remedy is buried in a dict dump.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `mine` argument is fetched as `log.clone_id(create=False)` and passed to `stranded_text`, but `_require` still calls `stranded_text` with `ls.clone` and `mine` in `stranded_text(item, ..., ls.clone, mine)`. The remainder of the change (cleanup.py) is the only place that defines the new `stranded_text` signature and the remedy decision. This part does not answer the previously reported `_stranded_lines`/dict-vs-text defect, because it does not touch `ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py` at all; the manifest still shows that file only adding `_stranded_lines`, while the change’s own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) reads the `stranded` status field as a list of dicts. If `_stranded_lines` still interpolates each element verbatim as a string in the strain shown in the prior finding, that test fails on the exact new behavior this change claims to add.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:29 (`_require`)

chunk_findings.detail: The function's docstring promises "the remedy is never one this clone would refuse", but that promise is not kept when `mine` is `None`. For example, in a clone with no clone id set (`log.clone_id(create=False)` returns `None`), if a removed item's lease is held by another clone, `stranded_text` receives `clone` non-empty but `mine=None`. The condition `clone and mine is not None and clone != mine` is false, so it falls through to the generic fix starting with `ddflow release <item>`. In that clone, `release` refuses because the lease is held by another clone, so the status/wait/merge/complete/heartbeat message advises a command that will be refused, contrary to the intent and docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cleanup.py:stranded_text

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim with `f"  [!] {t}"`, but the status field is a list of **dicts**, as the change's own JSON test requires (`rows[0]["item"]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`). Input: after Bob removes `T2` and Alice's live lease is present, JSON status has `{"stranded": [{"item": "T2", "holder": "alice", "text": "ddflow release T2"}]}`. Text `ddflow status` then renders `[!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': 'ddflow release T2'}` instead of the intended item-plus-message line. The added text-status assertion does not answer this because the raw dict repr also contains `"T2"`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `mine` argument is fetched as `log.clone_id(create=False)` and passed to `stranded_text`, but `_require` still calls `stranded_text` with `ls.clone` and `mine` in `stranded_text(item, ..., ls.clone, mine)`. The remainder of the change (cleanup.py) is the only place that defines the new `stranded_text` signature and the remedy decision. This part does not answer the previously reported `_stranded_lines`/dict-vs-text defect, because it does not touch `ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py` at all; the manifest still shows that file only adding `_stranded_lines`, while the change’s own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) reads the `stranded` status field as a list of dicts. If `_stranded_lines` still interpolates each element verbatim as a string in the strain shown in the prior finding, that test fails on the exact new behavior this change claims to add.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:29 (`_require`)

chunk_findings.detail: The function's docstring promises "the remedy is never one this clone would refuse", but that promise is not kept when `mine` is `None`. For example, in a clone with no clone id set (`log.clone_id(create=False)` returns `None`), if a removed item's lease is held by another clone, `stranded_text` receives `clone` non-empty but `mine=None`. The condition `clone and mine is not None and clone != mine` is false, so it falls through to the generic fix starting with `ddflow release <item>`. In that clone, `release` refuses because the lease is held by another clone, so the status/wait/merge/complete/heartbeat message advises a command that will be refused, contrary to the intent and docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cleanup.py:stranded_text

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim with `f"  [!] {t}"`, but the status field is a list of **dicts**, as the change's own JSON test requires (`rows[0]["item"]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`). Input: after Bob removes `T2` and Alice's live lease is present, JSON status has `{"stranded": [{"item": "T2", "holder": "alice", "text": "ddflow release T2"}]}`. Text `ddflow status` then renders `[!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': 'ddflow release T2'}` instead of the intended item-plus-message line. The added text-status assertion does not answer this because the raw dict repr also contains `"T2"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py:_stranded_lines

chunk_findings.detail: The text-status assertion is vacuous for the renderer defect: it only checks `"T2" in text + err`. Since the broken `_stranded_lines` prints the entire dict repr `{'item': 'T2', ...}`, that substring is present, so the test passes equally for the buggy raw-dict rendering and the intended formatted line. It should assert the rendered line uses `rows[0]["item"]`/`rows[0]["text"]` and does not print a Python dict repr.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if _MCP_CALL.get(): return "the MCP surface"` is placed **before** the `requested_agent` / `DDFLOW_AGENT` / `CLAUDECODE` checks, so it does not act as a fallback for the "no marker" case the intent describes — it overrides the more specific markers. `surfaces/mcp.py` already carries a per-call agent: `_parse` computes `per_call or self.agent` and `_invoke`/`_invoke_marked` pass that `agent` down (`return per_call or self.agent, per_call, args, bad`). Given an MCP tool call that carries `per_call = "alice"` (i.e. the client passed an agent for that call), `agent_marker("alice")` now returns `"the MCP surface"` instead of `"--agent alice"`; the same happens to a `DDFLOW_AGENT`/`CLAUDECODE`-marked call made over MCP. Because `agent_identity()` returns exactly this string as the caller's identity (`return "the MCP surface" if via_mcp else agent_marker(requested_agent)`), every MCP caller collapses to one indistinguishable identity, so any consumer that distinguishes agents by that value — audit/attribution of who performed an action, or a rule comparing the approving agent against the authoring agent — can no longer tell `alice` from `bob` for MCP-originated calls, whereas before this change such a call was identified by its explicit marker. The intent only claimed that an MCP call *with no* `--agent`/`DDFLOW_AGENT`/`CLAUDECODE` was wrongly treated as the operator; the ordering change also rewrites the calls that do carry one. Keeping the explicit markers and using MCP only as a fallback (e.g. `return agent_marker(requested_agent) or "the MCP surface"`) would fix the reported bug without discarding them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/identity.py:129 (agent_marker)

chunk_findings.detail: The new wrapper calls `_identity().via_mcp()`. `_identity` is the `ddflow.services.identity` module (whose new `via_mcp` is a plain module-level `@contextmanager`), and modules are not callable. On the first MCP tool invocation the call raises `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable` before any tool body runs; it should be `with _identity.via_mcp():`.

chunk_findings.detail: The test and the change's intent both scope the refusal to a live marker process "on this host", and the function is even named `..._judges_commit_liveness_and_host`, but the host dimension is never exercised. Every marker in the test comes from `RUN.mark_started(...)` on the current host, and the only mutations are `data["pid"]` / `data["pid_start"]` (lines 51-53 and 58-59); the `host` field is never read, changed to another host, or asserted on. Given a tree identity and a live marker written on host A, an implementation of `live_run` that drops or ignores the host comparison entirely (over-refusing a legitimate run of the same commit on host B, e.g. a shared/cluster worktree) still returns `None` for `tree-bbb`, `unit_tests`, `""` and a non-live pid, so all five assertions at lines 46, 54-57, 60 pass and the suite stays green. The untested input is simply a marker whose recorded host differs from the local one, which must yield `None`; no such input is constructed anywhere in this file (or in test 1, which only ever races an in-host process).

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal is a non-atomic check-then-act. If two `ddflow gate run` invocations for the same item/gate/commit start together, both can call `RUN.live_run` before either has called `RUN.mark_started`; both see no live twin and both proceed to write their markers and execute the same gate. That is precisely the concurrent same-commit duplicate the change is meant to refuse. The interleaving is: A:`live_run() -> None`, B:`live_run() -> None`, then both `mark_started()` and run. The check must be combined with `mark_started` under the same atomic section and re-checked after acquiring it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:629 (`RUN.live_run` before `RUN.mark_started` at line 681)

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added tests do not exercise the real CLI path for the claimed “newer commit stays allowed” behavior. The module docstring states “A run on a newer commit stays allowed,” but the only check for a different sha is `RUN.live_run(repo, "T1", "ci", "tree-bbb") is None`. An implementation of `gate run` that refuses _any_ second run on gate `T1` regardless of sha would still pass both new tests. To guard the requirement, a test must advance the commit and assert `run_cli(repo, "gate", "run", "T1", "unit_tests")` exits successfully while the first run is still live.
